Subject: MSA + Order Form — OS dependency indemnity carveout request

Hi Sara,

Thanks for the redlines — really appreciate the quick turnaround. One item we want to flag and discuss before legal sign-off: your legal team has added a broad indemnity carveout in the Order Form that excludes liability for any third-party IP claims arising from open-source components used by Helix.

To reduce risk for both sides, we propose the following approach:
- Redwood will accept a limited carveout for consumer-grade OSS (patch-level libs), but not for cases where Helix has (a) modified an open-source dependency in a way that introduces infringement, or (b) bundled third-party proprietary modules into the delivered integration.
- For any alleged third-party IP claim that appears tied to a Helix modification or third-party proprietary module, Helix would be responsible for defense and indemnity.

Can you confirm whether Helix will accept a modified carveout along the lines above? If helpful we can sketch specific language (short redline) and loop in legal to accelerate.

Thanks — can we aim to resolve this this week? We have an internal milestone tied to getting the MSA executed.

Best,
Hannah

Hi Hannah,

Appreciate the clear ask. Helix is trying to protect its procurement stack from broad indemnity exposure related to OSS we ship with our product. Our legal team is nervous about language that creates open-ended vendor liability when Helix ships integrations containing multiple third-party components.

That said, wethink the modified carveout you suggest is reasonable in principle. Our legal team would like to see concrete redline language that:
1) Defines "modified" vs "unmodified" OSS (we propose a simple definition: "modified" means any change to source code beyond packaging or configuration).
2) Adds a short notice-and-cure period (30 days) for alleged infringements tied to OSS before indemnity obligations trigger.
3) Limits vendor indemnity exposure to direct damages and defense costs (no consequential).

I'll push this to our legal lead and get back with a tracked redline.

Best,

Hannah — draft attached. Key points I implemented:

1) Definition: "Open-Source Software (OSS)" and "Modified OSS". I used simple language: "'Modified OSS' means source-level changes beyond packaging, configuration, or minor backporting that are not created by Redwood."
2) Notice & Cure: 30 days to investigate and (if applicable) remediate. During the cure period Redwood may temporarily disable the affected integration if necessary to mitigate risk.
3) Limitation on Damages: Redwood proposes vendor liability limited to direct costs of defense and settlements, and cap equal to the fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the prior 12 months. No consequential damages.

I'm attaching Helix_MSA_redline_v3.pdf (tracked changes) and a short plain-language summary you can send to Sara.

Open items I flagged in comments: whether to allow a joint defense option (we proposed to keep it optional) and whether Helix will accept the 12-month fees cap or wants a flat-dollar cap.

If we agree internally, Hannah — I can send to Helix legal tonight with a one-paragraph cover note.
